2. Send the request about title.txt. Read the proposed plan. After the change, inspect the changed lines and test the result.

4. Ask the helper which line gives the date. Look in both files for that line.

after: First run: The reply from Ask names fixture.csv and creates no patch. Second run: README gains Test command: python3 report.py. No other file changes.

rescuePrompt: Report where the input is documented. Leave the repository as you found it.

1. A repository keeps project files and their saved history. A commit is a saved checkpoint in a project. In a practice repository add report.py reads fixture.csv to README, commit it, and push to the practice branch. Select that repository in Devin Ask once its index includes the line.
2. Give Ask the request. Check its answer against README without making edits.
3. In Devin Agent select the same branch. Ask for a plan to add the separate line Test command: python3 report.py to README. Approve the one-line plan and ask Agent to apply it. Inspect the diff.

caption: Practice request
before: Plan a tiny change to loans.txt that illustrates the renewal rule with one allowed case. Keep the rule itself intact. Which file needs to change?
after: First run: First example allows one renewal with nobody waiting. Second run: Second example refuses renewal when a borrower waits. The earlier example still covers a loan with no waiting borrower.

rescuePrompt: Apply the original waiting-borrower condition to the second example and retain the original rule.

2. Send the renewal request to Agent, read the plan, and compare the proposed edit with loans.txt.

caption: Practice request
before: Build a tiny report that finds counts.csv beside its script and prints the total. Which command will let another session run this without a machine-specific path?
after: First run: 2 + 7 = 9 from the project folder. Second run: The parent-folder run also prints 9. Both starts reach the same data file.

caption: Practice request
before: Create a running score display. It starts at zero, accepts signed whole numbers and keeps all previous turns. Show the score after entries 5 and -2. What is the running score after each entry?
after: First run: 5 − 2 = 3. Second run: Undo removes -2 and restores 5. The previous turn is still on the score sheet.

rescue: If Undo clears all turns, ask for one history entry to be removed.
rescuePrompt: Keep earlier score entries and remove only the newest turn when Undo is pressed.

1. Start a Devin Agent session in a practice folder.
2. Submit the worked request about score, inspect the changed lines, and try the first two signed turns.
3. While reviewing the output, request Undo last turn. Try it once and inspect the changed files.

caption: Practice request
before: The written rule allows up to and including four guests. Demonstrate the failing boundary test, fix only that comparison, and show the test output on both versions. Which test detects the changed boundary?
after: First run: Four changes from refused to allowed. Second run: Five stays refused. The repaired rule admits four while leaving five outside the limit.

rescue: If the agent broadens every case, ask for the first disallowed count.
rescuePrompt: Test the value just outside the allowed range and show the comparison in the diff.

1. In a Devin practice repo create gate.py with one line: def allowed(n): return n < 4. Ask the agent for a plan and a test before editing.
2. Have Devin run the boundary test before and after the proposed edit. Read the comparison in the diff.
3. Review the diff. Test five guests after the fix as a control.

caption: Practice request
before: Draft a reusable report recipe that checks the headers, counts known entries including zero, and gives the sum. Try it on the supplied practice file. Report any missing count by its row ID.
after: First run: 2 known entries with total 2. Second run: 1 known entry with total 2 and b reported missing. The missing value has no part in the sum.

rescuePrompt: Mark the status of each Count field before adding it to the report.

caption: Practice request
before: Build a local simulation. Ticket D7 revision one is delivered twice, with a different delivery ID each time. Keep one session per ticket and apply each revision once. Which session records should exist?
after: First run: One session S1 for D7, with revision one recorded once. Second run: S1 contains revisions one and two once each. The session count stays at one.

rescue: If revision two creates another session for D7, ask for the ticket-to-session lookup.
rescuePrompt: Look up the session by ticket ID. Within that session apply each unseen revision once even when delivery IDs differ.

2. Run the two deliveries using session S1 for D7. Inspect the session list and applied revisions.

caption: Practice request
before: Repo grant: read. Project role: reviewer. Requested action: push a change. Explain which permission prevents a push and what useful work can still be done.
after: First run: Push blocked by the read-only repo grant. Second run: Reading README fits the grant. The permission still blocks writes.

caption: Practice request
before: Runner A can read the practice repo. Only Runner B can reach the file store. A report needs both. Show where this deployment path stops and label the missing connection.
after: First run: A lacks the file store and B lacks the project folder. Second run: B can read both inputs needed for this project folderrt. The report needs both the project and the file store.

caption: Practice request
before: Model starting an offline mock session. A start returns S4; a status lookup for S4 returns running. Store that ID and poll it without requesting a second session. Show the call sequence. Which request can reuse the first job?
after: First run: One start, followed by status for S4. Second run: Finished on S4. The start count stays at one. The final status belongs to the original session.

caption: Practice request
before: Both projects have a local Help button. Plan a two-project change to the label Guide. Keep a separate test result per project; Shelf already passed and Desk has no result yet. Which project still blocks the fleet? Give the starting release status for both projects.
after: First run: Shelf passed and Desk is untested. Second run: Shelf and Desk each have their own passing result. The two checks name different projects.

rescuePrompt: List Shelf and Desk separately with the exact test result supplied for each.

1. Select practice projects Shelf and Desk in Devin. Keep each project’s test evidence separate.
2. Send the label-change plan request. Read the separate Shelf and Desk statuses before declaring the release ready.
3. A repository keeps project files and their saved history. Give Devin this update: Desk passed. Update the two-project status note and say whether a project still blocks release.

caption: Practice request
before: Session A used 4 units for accepted fix P1. B used 3 on the same P1. C used 2 on a declined fix. What was the cost per distinct accepted fix?
after: First run: (4 + 3 + 2) ÷ 1 = 9 units per accepted fix. Second run: 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5 units per accepted fix. The same nine units now cover two accepted fixes.
why: Nine units bought one accepted fix in the first run. It makes no difference that two sessions worked on that one fix.
rescue: If three sessions become three wins, ask to group by accepted fix ID.
rescuePrompt: List the distinct accepted fix IDs before dividing total units.
try:
1. Start in Devin Ask with the fictional session ledger. Keep estimated cost separate from the number of accepted changes.
2. Ask for the total use and distinct accepted fixes. Check whether retries for P1 are counted correctly.
3. Change C to an accepted separate fix P2 and recompute from the same units.

premise: Optional live extension to the checkout case. Use Devin Agent to build and test the fee ledger.

rescuePrompt: Use the ticket identifier to find the existing charge before adding a new fee.

caption: Practice request
before: A locker charges 2 credits per started hour, capped at 5 credits per visit. A stay lasts 61 minutes. What is the charge? Show where the rounding happens.
after: First run: 2 started hours × 2 = 4 credits. Second run: 4 started hours × 2 = 8, capped at 5 credits. The displayed fee reaches the cap.

rescuePrompt: Round up the hours, multiply by the rate, then take the smaller of that bill and the visit cap.
try:
1. Start a new ChatGPT chat. Record the mode shown near the message field or record default if there is no choice.

caption: Practice request
before: Classify each slip as ROOM or MAIL. ROOM means a room reservation; MAIL means a delivery problem. Boat Hall needs a booking. Parcel did not arrive. Return one label per slip, in order.
after: First run: ROOM, MAIL. Second run: ROOM, ROOM. Both labels now match the room rule.

rescuePrompt: Emit only the ordered labels, with no heading or commentary.

caption: Practice request
before: From the attached table, report the number of known seat counts and their total. Explain how you treated the empty cell and the recorded zero.
after: First run: 3 known; 3 + 0 + 5 = 8. Second run: 4 known; 3 + 2 + 0 + 5 = 10. The zero still counts as a known value.

rescue: If the first count says four, ask for a row-by-row inclusion check.
rescuePrompt: Mark each seat value included or missing before computing the count and sum.

caption: Practice request
before: Build a single-file book index with entries Harbor and Orchard. A search box filters the titles. Include a Clear button. Show which file changes, and how to check the search by hand. Which action should restore both titles?
after: First run: Har leaves Harbor visible. Second run: The Clear button restores Harbor and Orchard. The search box is empty again.

rescuePrompt: Test the Clear handler in the generated page and show how the visible list changes.

2. Build the index from the request. Open index.html and enter har to check the first search result.

caption: Practice request
before: Create a badge for a fictional coach. Place a white whistle inside a navy circle. Leave an empty ribbon underneath for a name. The background outside the badge should be plain. Which symbols are visible on the badge?
after: First run: White whistle, navy circle, empty ribbon. Second run: Gold whistle, navy circle, empty ribbon. Only the whistle changes color.

rescuePrompt: Remove the lettering from the ribbon while preserving the whistle color and the navy circle.

1. Choose image creation in ChatGPT. Keep the first result open for the edit.

caption: Practice request
before: Using the current Shift note, report the early start time and the words that support it. Does the document also give an end time?
after: First run: 07:30, end time unspecified. Second run: 07:30 to noon, supported by the added line. The start time still comes from the original note.

rescue: If the old answer persists, ask which document version it used.
rescuePrompt: Read the current Shift note and quote the sentence containing the end time.

caption: Practice request
before: Thread in time order: “Tuesday works.” Then “Could we switch to Wednesday?” Finally “Tuesday is confirmed.” Draft the decision line for the meeting notes. Which day was approved?
after: First run: Tuesday is confirmed; Wednesday was a request. Second run: Wednesday is confirmed by the final reply. The earlier suggestion now has a decision behind it.
why: A proposed meeting date stays tentative until a later message accepts it.
rescue: If a suggestion becomes a decision too soon, ask for the accepting message.
rescuePrompt: Quote the last explicit confirmation before drafting the meeting decision.
try:
1. Start a Copilot Chat conversation with these fictional thread lines. Keep the order of the messages.
2. Submit the practice thread and identify the message supporting each decision in Copilot’s answer.
3. Replace the last line with “Wednesday is confirmed.” Request a revised decision line.

caption: Practice request
before: Draft a slide headline about support among respondents. Give the fraction and identify the group in the number you divide by. Do not imply that all invitees replied.
after: First run: 6 of 9 respondents, about 67%. Second run: 6 of 12 invitees, 50%. The six yes votes stay the same.
why: Changing the headline's audience changes the number you divide by even when the supporting votes stay fixed.
rescue: If both headlines say 67%, ask which group each describes.
rescuePrompt: Write each headline as six out of a named group before converting it to a percentage.
try:
1. Create a practice Word document and open Copilot beside it. Enter “12 invited, 9 replied, 6 would return.”.
2. Use the practice request to make the outline. Compare each slide claim with the brief before keeping it.
3. Change the requested audience measure to support among all invitees. Compare the resulting headline.

caption: Practice request
before: Give a formula for the Dock subtotal using the Team and Units columns of the current table. Keep the source rows visible. Which two entries contribute?
after: First run: Dock subtotal 4 + 2 = 6. Second run: Dock subtotal 4 + 5 = 9. Only the edited Dock entry changes the subtotal.
why: A live formula responds to an edit in the source table without another chat reply.
rescue: If the number stays six, ask for cell references.
rescuePrompt: Replace the typed subtotal with a formula over the table columns filtered to Dock.
try:
1. In a practice Excel workbook create a table with columns Team and Units. Enter Dock 4, Gate 3, Dock 2. Open Copilot in Excel.
2. Ask Copilot for the Dock formula. Enter it in a result cell and inspect the subtotal in the workbook.

caption: Practice request
before: Use the ticket handbook to answer a visitor asking where to return an unused ticket. Identify the source. Give no refund estimate unless the handbook supplies one.
after: First run: Blue desk, supported by the handbook. Second run: Cash refund policy unknown. The handbook has no rule promising a cash refund.
why: A handbook agent needs a way to stop when its source is silent.
rescue: If it offers a refund amount, ask for the exact policy line.
rescuePrompt: Answer only from the ticket handbook. State when a requested policy is absent.
try:
1. In a permitted Copilot agent workspace create a practice handbook helper. Give it a source reading “Return unused tickets at the blue desk.”.
2. Give the handbook helper the policy question. Compare its reply to the named rule in the approved practice material.
3. Ask whether the desk issues cash refunds. Inspect the evidence it offers.

caption: Practice request
before: Meeting note: “Stage crew brings the lamp. Desk crew signs it in.” Turn the note into a short handoff with one action and owner on each line. Which part of the meeting note still applies?
after: First run: Stage brings; Desk signs in. Second run: Desk brings and signs in. Stage has no job in the new version.
why: Revising the same handoff exposes a stale owner that can survive a polished rewrite.
rescue: If Stage still appears, ask to trace both actions to the latest note.
rescuePrompt: Use only the revised note and list the named owner beside each action.
try:
1. In a Muse workspace start a draft from the fictional meeting note. Use the same draft for the edit.
2. Give Muse the meeting note and ask for a saved handoff. Open the draft and check the owner on each line.
3. Change the note so the desk crew brings the lamp too. Revise the stored draft and compare the ownership.

caption: Request for Gemini
before: My bag note reads hat, pencil, hat, cup. Make a list in the order I first named each item. Which item appeared twice but needs only one place on the list?
after: First run: Three lines in order: hat, pencil, cup. Second run: Hat, pencil, cup, mitt. Each appears at its first position.
why: Removing the second hat keeps the first hat where the packer put it.
rescue: The second hat appears again or mitt is lost. Ask for a correction.
rescuePrompt: Include mitt once at the end and keep the first appearance of each other item.
try:
1. Open Gemini and choose a new chat.
2. Send the request about hat.
3. Count the lines. Put a tick beside each item in the note as you read the answer.
4. Append cup and mitt to the original note and run it again.

caption: Request for Gemini
before: My three turns are Blue, Red and Gold. Blue goes after Red; Gold goes before Red. Give their order and point to the clue that places Gold.
after: First run: Gold, Red, Blue satisfies both rules. Only passing answers count. Second run: Red, Blue, Gold. Blue follows Red and Gold follows Blue.
why: A changed order must still obey both position clues.
rescue: The order puts Gold before Blue even after its clue changes. Ask for a correction.
rescuePrompt: Trace each before or after relation and put the three teams in that order.
try:
1. Open a fresh Gemini chat. Tap the model name. Choose a thinking level if your account offers it.
2. Send the request about Gold.
3. Try the same request in a new chat at another available level. Check both lists with three paper slips.
4. Replace Gold goes before Red with Gold goes after Blue. Ask for the new order.

caption: Request for Gemini
before: I drew A in the left circle and C in the right circle. The middle is empty. Read my two existing labels back. Where should B go to make the letters run in order?
after: First run: B belongs in the middle. C is on the right. Second run: The middle circle is empty. The right circle still holds C.
why: A transcript can confuse the label of a circle with its position.
rescue: The voice reply still puts B in the middle after you move it. Ask for a correction.
rescuePrompt: Describe each position from left to right using the current picture.
try:
1. Start Gemini Live on your tablet and turn on its microphone.
2. Say the worked example about circle aloud. Listen to the reply before asking again.
3. Listen to the letters it repeats. Change your question to ask which circle holds C.
4. A transcript is a written copy of spoken words. Move B from the middle to the left and erase A. Show the drawing again. Ask which circle is empty.

caption: Request for Gemini
before: Here is a riddle about keys that open no locks. The answer is piano. Give me one hint now. Wait until I say Reveal before naming the instrument. Which clue will you start with?
after: First run: The hint leaves piano out. The second reply says piano and links the keys to music. Second run: The first hint withholds piano. The later reveal names piano and explains its keys.
why: The Gem has to remember whether you have asked for a hint or a reveal.
rescue: The first hint gives away the piano. Ask for a correction.
rescuePrompt: Hold the answer back until my reveal request. Give one clue about music.
try:
1. Use Gemini on the web. Open Gems, choose to make a Gem, give it a short name, add your rules and save.
2. In Gems, save the standing rule from this lab. Start a chat with your Gem and give it the worked example about riddle.
3. Ask for a hint, then type Reveal. Check the two replies separately.
4. Start a new game with the same riddle. Ask for a hint before asking for the solution.

caption: Request for Gemini
before: I want a tiny tap game. My Score button starts at zero and each tap adds one. At three, show You won. Give me Reset so I can play from zero again.
after: First run: 0 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 and the win appears only at three. Second run: The Reset button shows 0 and clears the win. Two taps give 0 + 1 + 1 = 2 with no winner.
why: A third tap must win exactly once even if you keep tapping.
rescue: Reset leaves the win message visible on the second tap. Ask for a correction.
rescuePrompt: Check the score on both sides of the winning threshold, including after Reset.
try:
1. In a new Gemini chat, open Canvas. Send the worked request about Score and open Preview.
2. Tap Score twice and read the counter. Tap once more and look for the win message.
3. Press Reset and tap Score twice. Read the new score and check whether the win message is visible.

caption: Request for Gemini
before: My selected source is named Schedule. It says practice starts at 2 and to bring a pencil. Which time does it give, and which exact line supports your answer?
after: First run: The answer is 2. The line about the pencil supplies no time. Second run: 3 is supported by the new start-time sentence. The pencil sentence still gives no time.

rescuePrompt: Point to the sentence that actually contains the practice time.
try:
1. Create a notebook in Gemini Notebook. Add the Schedule note from this lab as a source.
2. Select Schedule and send the worked request to Notebook chat.

4. A citation points to the source of an answer. Replace the source with Practice starts at 3. Bring a pencil. Select only that source and repeat the time question.

caption: Request for Gemini
before: My kit needs two red flags, one blue flag and three cones. Give me a packing list that keeps the two colors separate. How many things will I put in the bag?
after: First run: Three lines list red flags 2, blue flag 1 and cones 3. Total items packed would be 6. Second run: 2 red flags + 1 blue flag + 1 cone = 4 items. 2 + 1 + 3 = 6.

rescue: The total falls but the list still packs three cones. Ask for a correction.
rescuePrompt: Count each named supply separately before adding the packed items.
try:
1. Open Gemini. Choose Task mode and start a fresh task. Use the task thread to see its work.
2. Send the request about flags.

caption: Request for Gemini
before:
I am using an iPad for Notebook flashcards. Plan how to look up creating a deck, flipping a card and trying missed cards.

My device is an iPad and my study deck is in Gemini Notebook.

Which Google help page supports each iPad action?
after: First run: The cited iPad guide places flashcards in Studio and says to tap a card to flip it. Second run: The iPad guide describes a missed-card set at the end of the deck. The answer links to that guide.
why: Reviewing the research plan can catch an excursion into pricing before the search starts.

1. Open Gemini and choose Deep Research from the tools menu. Enter the question, then inspect the plan before starting.
2. Send the request about iPad.
3. Run the edited plan, open its cited mobile guide and locate Flashcards and Quizzes in App.
4. Narrow the follow-up to reviewing misses. Compare the answer against Flashcards and Quizzes in App.

caption: Request for Gemini
before: My selected notes are Rules and Round. Rules says a star earns two points; Round gives Blue three stars. Give the total and a citation for each part of the math.
after: First run: Rules gives 2. Round gives 3. Blue earned 6 points. Second run: 4 stars × 2 points = 8. The four comes from Round. 3 × 2 = 6.
why: Two citations serve different jobs when one states the scoring rule and the other records the turn.
rescue: The score changes without a citation to the new Round note. Ask for a correction.
rescuePrompt: Cite Rules for the multiplier and Round for the number of stars.
try:
1. Open Gemini Notebook. Make a fresh notebook. Add each sample note as a separate source with its own title.
2. Add the named notes from this lab as separate sources and select them. Use the request about stars with those notes.
3. Open both citations. Multiply the score for one star by the number drawn.
4. A citation points to the source of an answer. Replace Round with Blue drew four stars. Keep Rules selected. Ask for the revised score.

caption: Request for Gemini
before:
Old and New are dated game notes. Give the winning score and date in each source.

Old — May 1. Players earn one point per turn. The first to 8 wins.
New — May 4. Players earn one point per turn. This replaces the old target. The first to 12 wins.

Which rule changed and which rule about earning a point stayed the same?
after: First run: Both sheets give one point per turn. The May 1 target is 8. The May 4 sheet replaces it with 12. Second run: Old supports 8. The replacement target of 12 is absent from the selection.
why: Deselecting a revised rule changes what the selected notebook can support.
rescue: The notebook cites the revised target after New has been deselected. Ask for a correction.
rescuePrompt: Trace the stated target to one of the currently selected sheets.

2. Give the clean practice lines and the worked request to the approved chat. Check which line actually records a state.

caption: Request for the practice case
before: My handoff says Box A was delayed at minute 0 and arrived at minute 5 through a new relay. My case excerpt ends at SN4. Give the retry result and state with their evidence. What changes when I supply SN5?
after: First run: The retry reached Box A through the new relay. Through SN4 the case is still Open. Second run: The handoff shows five minutes between attempts and a later Closed entry. The handoff contains only the practice labels.
why: A new reader can check the times and the case state from the cleaned note. The original address adds nothing to that test.
rescue: If they need the alias key to answer, ask for a targeted follow-up.
rescuePrompt: Check that both the cleaned copy and the receipt use evidence labels consistently and contain no original IDs.
try:
1. Open the three local practice files. Use SP2 and SP5 to check that the tool and use are allowed. Only the cleaned practice lines go in the message.
2. In the approved practice chat, send the handoff with the case excerpt through SN4. Read the state and the time between deliveries.

caption: Practice request
before: Prepare a release note from these results. Candidate label 1.1 runs locally. The published test still shows 1.0. Which version can I describe as live, and which has passed only locally?
after: First run: 1.0 live; 1.1 tested locally. Second run: 1.1 verified at the published address for scoring and reset. The note now names a check at the same address a player opens.
why: Testing a file in a folder does not tell you which version a reader opened from a bookmark.
rescue: If the candidate is marked live early, ask for the test location.
rescuePrompt: Tie every status in the release note to the location where that version was observed.
try:
1. Open the Signal Sprint sample from the shipping lab. Keep two local copies in separate practice folders.
2. Apply the practice request to the supplied sample results. Keep the local test and the public observation on separate lines.
3. Replace the published result with “1.1, scoring and reset both passed at the published address.” Rewrite the note.

caption: Practice request
before: A harmless practice marker was committed in version one and removed in version two. A reader downloads only version two; a maintainer also clones the history. Which copy can still show the old marker?
after: First run: The maintainer can find the marker in history; the current game omits it. Second run: The current game and its history both contain it. Removing a marker from one version leaves earlier versions readable.
why: Deleting a line from the working file leaves a different exposure surface in earlier commits.
rescue: If the first version is called erased, ask which commit was inspected.
rescuePrompt: Distinguish the current HTML from earlier snapshots when reporting marker visibility.
try:
1. Inspect the game file and its local Git history in a disposable practice folder. Use only a harmless marker.
2. Compare the current file and its saved history. Use the request to explain who can still see the harmless marker.
3. In a separate practice folder, leave the marker in version two. Repeat the comparison without publishing anything.

caption: Request for the practice case
before: For my local Signal Sprint game, give the expected score after a miss, two hits and a late tap. It starts at zero with fifteen seconds. Which tap stops counting?
after: First run: A miss changes neither score nor target. Two correct taps give 2 points and switch the target each time. Second run: At zero the answers lock. Restart begins at 0 points and 15 seconds. A miss and two hits score 0 + 1 + 1 = 2.
why: The last-second test catches a scoring button that stays active after the clock reaches zero.
rescue: A late tap may slip into the first score of a replay. Ask for a closer check.
rescuePrompt: Trace the final tick, late tap and restart as three separate actions. Give the visible score after each.
try:
1. Open the local Signal Sprint game. Give a practice chat the timing request and keep its prediction beside the game.
2. Try one miss and two hits. Move the clock down to zero, then try one more tap.
3. Press Restart. Read the score and clock, and compare both with the prediction.

caption: Request for the practice case
before: My practice folder holds the tested game in index.html. Give a Git sequence that saves just that file as the first checkpoint and lets me see exactly what was saved.
after: First run: Only index.html is staged for this first commit. Second run: The latest log shows the game checkpoint. The final short status is empty.
why: Checking the staged list shows exactly which game file will travel in the next checkpoint.
rescue: If Git says there is nothing to commit, ask for a targeted follow-up.
rescuePrompt: Inspect the latest log and file list before trying again. Do not invent an extra edit.
try:
1. In a blank practice project, place the tested index.html game. Use the lab’s local Git setup commands.
2. A diff shows which lines changed. Give the checkpoint request to a practice chat. Compare the proposed file list with git diff --cached --name-only after staging index.html.
3. A commit is a saved checkpoint in a project. Commit the game file. Read the latest short commit ID and run git status --short.

caption: Request for the practice case
before: My practice game is at version 1.0. I want to try only a new 1.1 label and then undo that change while keeping both steps in history. What version will the player see?
after: First run: The candidate shows 1.1 with the same game rules. Second run: The rollback creates its own history entry. The restored game shows 1.0 and the final workspace is clean.
why: A separate undo commit records both the trial release and the decision to return to the old label.
rescue: If the newest commit or status differs, ask for a targeted follow-up.
rescuePrompt: Inspect the history and stop. This exercise assumes HEAD is exactly the small label edit.
try:
1. In the clean spare Git project, start with the saved 1.0 game. Give a practice chat the request for the 1.1 trial.
2. A commit is a saved checkpoint in a project. Edit only the displayed label to 1.1. Check the changed lines, commit the file and play the sample game.
3. A rollback puts the old setting back. Use the lab’s git revert command on that trial commit. Read the label, the recent history and the short status.

caption: Request for the practice case
before: My local practice game once held the harmless label PRACTICE_MARKER. I removed it in a later save. Which Git views show the current file and the older copy?
after: First run: The current file has no marker. The earlier commit still contains it. Second run: The public game needs no service key. Any later private service call belongs on a protected server with access checks.
why: Removing a pretend marker from the current HTML does not erase the test marker from older commits.
rescue: If the AI suggests hiding a key in HTML, ask for a targeted follow-up.
rescuePrompt: Distinguish the current file from its earlier commit. Use the harmless practice marker to explain why both must be checked.
try:
1. In a spare local folder, use the lab’s harmless PRACTICE_MARKER text and save the first version with Git.
2. A commit is a saved checkpoint in a project. Remove the marker and commit again. Give a practice chat the question about the two versions. Search the current file and the older commit.
3. Sketch where the browser ends and a private server begins. Mark which side may hold a real service credential. Keep the example free of real credentials.

caption: Request for the practice case
before: I have Signal Sprint version 1.0 in my release folder. Give me a local browser test that checks the game opens directly. What version and score should appear after I finish a round and restart?
after: First run: The local address opens Signal Sprint directly. The game shows version 1.0. Second run: The score is back at zero. The opening screen still shows version 1.0.
why: Opening the local address checks the game you will share. It lets you catch a folder listing before release.
rescue: If the local address shows a file list, ask how to reach the game in its release folder.
rescuePrompt: My local address opens a list of files. Where must index.html be for the server to show Signal Sprint at its opening address?
try:
1. In a spare folder, put the Signal Sprint release in index.html. Start the local server from the lab.
2. Open the local address and check the version on the game. Reload the address directly.
3. Play a round and press Restart. Record the version and score shown by this local copy.

caption: Request for the practice case
before: My old Signal Sprint copy says 0.9 and the release says 1.0. Give me a local test for two correct taps, the final tick, a late tap and Restart. What stays in the score?
after: First run: The old control shows 0.9. The tested release shows 1.0. Second run: After two correct picks, the score is 2 at one second and at zero. A late tap cannot add another point. Restart returns to 0 and 15 seconds. 15 − 14 = 1 second before the final tick. Two hits earn 2 points even after the late tap.
why: The version on the opening screen tells you which game the score test actually used.
rescue: If only the local test ran, ask for a targeted follow-up.
rescuePrompt: Mark the public address untested. If a label passed but the lock failed, record both. A correct title does not repair a broken timer.
try:
1. Serve the old 0.9 copy and the new 1.0 copy in their own practice folders. Read the version on each opening screen.
2. Play two correct turns on 1.0. Advance to one second left, then to zero. Try one late tap.
3. Press Restart. Read both the timer and score at the start of the new round.

caption: Practice request
before: A queue paused at 09:00. One test message arrived at 09:12. No other routes were tested. Write an update with headings Observed and Still unknown. Can the desk declare every route healthy?
after: First run: One message arrived at 09:12 and the other routes are untested. Second run: Two routes have a passing test. The remaining routes still lack a test.
why: When new mail arrives, the handoff can change. An untested route still needs its own receipt.
rescue: A claim that mail is fixed everywhere goes past the evidence. Ask for a narrower update.
rescuePrompt: Count the passing route tests. Describe other routes as untested and leave their individual names unspecified.
try:
1. Start a new chat in Claude.
2. Ask Claude for Observed and Still unknown. Check each line against the queue note.
3. Tell Claude that a second route has now passed. Ask what is still unknown.

caption: Practice request
before: Training requests: dock closed, gate open, stores closed. Using the project handbook, report the weekly count and identify the rule by revision.
after: First run: Dock and stores count, so 1 + 1 = 2. The rule comes from revision B. Second run: One closed request counts under revision B. The two open requests stay out.
why: A project file earns its place when a second conversation can use its rule without another upload.
rescue: If the answer counts the open gate request, ask it to locate the saved rule.
rescuePrompt: Find the counting rule in Handbook. Give its revision and apply it only to closed requests.
try:
1. In Claude Projects create Practice desk. Add a text file called Handbook containing: Revision B. Count only closed requests in the weekly total.
2. Use a chat inside Practice desk. Ask for the count, then find the revision and rule in Handbook.
3. Start another chat inside that same project. Ask about two open requests and one closed request. Leave the handbook attached to the project.

caption: Practice request
before: Make an interactive ticket tally that starts at zero. Include Count and Reset buttons. Each press of Count adds exactly one. Keep the total visible. What file or preview can I try?
after: First run: 0 + 1 + 1 = 2 tickets before Reset. Second run: The Reset button shows 0. One new press gives 1 ticket.
why: The first press after a reset checks whether the button also cleared the value stored behind the display.
rescue: If the new press shows 3, ask for a change to the stored tally.
rescuePrompt: Reset the saved count as well as its label. Test two clicks, a reset and one more click.
try:
1. Start a new Claude chat with access to interactive Artifacts.
2. Generate the interactive tally from the request. Open the Artifact and locate its count and reset controls.
3. In the Artifact preview tap Count twice. Then tap Reset and Count once more.

caption: Practice request
before: Inspect index.html and plan a label-only edit. Change Clear All to Reset. Keep the starting score and the button action intact. Which lines would change?
after: First run: The diff changes Clear All to Reset. The starting score is 2. Second run: Pressing The Reset button shows 0. Reloading the original page starts it at 2.
why: A label change is small enough to check separately from the counter behind it.
rescue: If the diff also changes the starting value, ask for a smaller edit.
rescuePrompt: Keep the original starting score of 2 and existing click action. Limit the change to the button label.
try:
1. Save the chapter’s starter HTML as index.html in a practice folder. Open that folder in Claude Code.
2. In Claude Code submit the label-only request. Approve the planned label edit and inspect the diff.
3. A diff shows which lines changed. Read the diff in Claude Code. Run the page, press Reset and reload it to test the initial score again.

caption: Practice request
before: Locate Shift card through the approved connector. What does the first line say? Identify the document you actually read. If it cannot be opened, report missing access.
after: First run: A successful read returns Window B from Shift card. Second run: A successful new read returns Window C from the same document. Missing access leaves the test blocked.
why: Changing Shift card gives a second read something new to find. Quoting the old value would miss the edit.
rescue: If the reply guesses a window without opening the item, ask for a traceable result.
rescuePrompt: Identify the Shift card document you opened. Quote the first line, or report that access failed.
try:
1. Create a document named Shift card in an approved practice Drive folder. Give it one line reading Window B. Connect the approved service in Claude and start a new chat.
2. A connector links two systems and controls what can pass between them. Send only the lookup request. Keep Window B in the Drive document. If the connector cannot open it, record Blocked and leave the second run pending.
3. Change the line in the source document to Window C. Start a new Claude chat and ask it to read Shift card again.

caption: Practice request
before: Read the open practice desk without changing it. Which label sits beside 8? Tell me whether you read that value from the page or inferred it.
after: First run: 8 belongs to waiting requests. Second run: The next check is 10:30. The unused Submit button stays untouched.
why: Two different readings on the same page show the difference between seeing a control and acting on it.
rescue: If the helper volunteers to submit anything, ask it to stay in reading mode.
rescuePrompt: Report only the waiting label and the visible next-check time. Leave every control alone.

1. Open the chapter’s practice desk in Chrome. Open Claude in Chrome on that tab and leave Submit alone.
2. Ask Claude to identify the label beside 8. Watch the desk page while it answers.
3. Expand Show next check yourself. Ask Claude to read the newly visible time without pressing Submit.

caption: Practice request
before: Every Monday at 09:00 UTC remind me that desk B is on duty. Report the saved weekday, reminder text and time zone so I can check the schedule.
after: First run: Monday at 09:00 UTC with a reminder about desk B. Second run: Tuesday at 09:00 UTC with the same reminder. Only the weekday changes.
why: The saved day and time are something you can check again after closing the chat.
rescue: If the wording sounds right but there is no saved task, ask where to inspect it.
rescuePrompt: Identify the saved reminder entry and its next run. If no task was created, say that clearly.
try:
1. Open scheduled tasks in Claude Cowork with a practice account. Choose to create a task.
2. UTC is one shared clock. It lets you compare times from different places. Enter the worked request about reminder when creating the task. Check the saved task list for its weekday and UTC time.
3. Edit the practice task to Tuesday at the same time. Inspect the next run and remove the test task afterward.

caption: Practice request
before: Before lunch there were fifteen waiting items. After lunch there were five. Give a spoken handoff and then list the starting and ending counts in order.
after: First run: The transcript gives 15 first and 5 second. Second run: The revised pair is 15 and 9. The first count stays as spoken.
why: Checking the transcript catches a misheard teen number before it becomes a handoff.
rescue: If the transcript says fifty, ask for a digit-by-digit check.
rescuePrompt: The starting number is one five, fifteen. Keep it first and repeat the updated ending count separately.
try:
1. A transcript is a written copy of spoken words. Start a new Claude voice conversation, allow the microphone and speak the practice message. Read the transcript after your turn.
2. Speak the counts in the request. Stop and check the digits in Claude’s written transcript.
3. Say that the ending count was nine, not five. Check which number changed in the transcript.

caption: Practice request
before: Read the two rows in the attached practice PDF. Give each label and value, then calculate their combined count. Flag any cell you cannot read.
after: First run: The open count of 2 plus Closed 3 gives 5. Second run: The open count of 2 plus Closed 4 gives 6. Only the closed row increases.
why: A wrong sum is easier to trace when you can see which PDF row supplied each count.
rescue: If the total changes but the rows are missing, ask for the evidence.
rescuePrompt: Transcribe each row label and its number from the attached PDF before adding them.
try:
1. Create a practice PDF with lines Open 2 and Closed 3. Attach it in a new Claude chat.
2. Ask about the attached PDF. Compare the returned row labels and values with the two printed lines.
3. Make a second PDF with Open 2 and Closed 4. Attach it in a new chat and repeat the file question.

caption: Practice request
before: At 08:04 delivery was attempted. A retry began at 08:06. The log ends there. Which facts belong under Observed, and what belongs under Unknown?
after: First run: Observed contains the attempt and retry. Final delivery is unknown. Second run: Observed now includes delivery at 08:10. Final delivery can leave Unknown.
why: An extra timestamp should change the conclusion only when its event actually confirms delivery.
rescue: If the retry is described as success, ask for the exact confirming line.
rescuePrompt: Separate starting a retry from completing delivery. Name the line that supports a final result, or say unknown.
try:
1. Start a new Gemini chat and keep the training note and question in one message.
2. Give Gemini the short delivery log. Check the Observed and Unknown headings against the final recorded event.
3. Append Final delivery confirmed at 08:10 and ask for the two headings again.

caption: Practice request
before: When does the trial start and when does the wider rollout start? Cite the selected notebook source for each answer. Use undecided where the source does.
after: First run: Tuesday comes from Pilot and undecided comes from Rollout. Second run: The selected source still says wider rollout undecided. It supplies no trial date.
why: Removing Pilot removes the only source for Tuesday. It does not set a different day.
rescue: If Tuesday survives without a selected source, ask for a grounded answer.
rescuePrompt: Answer from the selected sources only. Which selected passage gives the trial date? If none does, mark it unknown.
try:
1. Create a Gemini Notebook. Add two copied-text sources named Pilot and Rollout. Pilot says Trial starts Tuesday. Rollout says Wider rollout undecided. Select both.
2. A citation points to the source of an answer. Ask the notebook for both dates. Open each citation to see which selected note actually supplies the answer.
3. Deselect Pilot, keep Rollout selected and ask the same question. Open the citation in each run.

caption: Practice request
before: Build a packed-bag counter in Canvas. Show a number starting at zero. Add bag increases it by one. Start over clears it. What can I press to begin a new count?
after: First run: 0 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 bags. Second run: The new tally starts at 0. The next bag makes 1.
why: Exercising the preview tests a working Canvas counter rather than a picture of one.
rescue: If the buttons look right but do nothing, ask for a working click action.
rescuePrompt: Connect each button to the displayed count. Run three adds, clear, then one add in the preview.
try:
1. Start a new Gemini chat and choose Canvas.
2. Generate the packed-bag counter. Open Preview and identify Add bag and Start over.
3. Press Add bag three times, then Start over. Press Add bag once after clearing.

caption: Practice request
before: Build a local score summary in the practice folder. An empty list displays No plays. A list containing one score of zero displays the number 0. Add a test for each case.
after: First run: The empty list shows No plays and the one-score list containing zero shows 0. Second run: The new list containing 3 shows 3. The original empty and zero tests both still pass.
why: A check for an empty list has to count entries, since a perfectly good entry can equal zero.
rescue: If zero disappears, ask the agent to test list length.
rescuePrompt: Distinguish an empty list from one containing zero. Keep both tests and show the changed lines.
try:
1. Open an empty practice folder as a project in Antigravity. In the agent panel ask to see the plan before edits.
2. A diff shows which lines changed. Ask the Antigravity agent to build and run the empty and zero tests. Read the diff before adding a third case.
3. Inspect the diff and run both tests. Add a separate input containing 3, and rerun the empty, zero and three-score cases.

caption: Practice request
before: Find Supply list through the connected service. Which item has a count of 4? Identify the source document or tell me that you could not read it.
after: First run: The source is Supply list and the item is paper rolls with count 4, or access is unavailable. Second run: A fresh read shows 6 for paper rolls. A response of 4 is stale.
why: Checking the document name catches an answer drawn from a different supply list.
rescue: If the reply supplies an unlabeled number, ask where it came from.
rescuePrompt: Identify the actual document and quote the current paper-roll line. Report unavailable if access failed.
try:
1. In an approved practice document called Supply list write Paper rolls: 4. Enable the permitted Connected App, then start a Gemini chat.
2. Ask for Supply list through the connector. Keep the count in the source document and check whether the item opens.
3. Edit the source to Paper rolls: 6. Ask Gemini to find the document again in a new chat.

caption: Practice request
before: Find the time inside Show next check on the open practice desk. Expand only that control if needed. Stop before Submit. What time do you see?
after: First run: The expanded panel shows 10:30. Submit stays unused. Second run: The visible waiting count is 8. The time panel can remain closed.
why: The two tasks have different action limits even though they use the same practice page.
rescue: If the browser plan includes Submit, stop it and ask for the smaller action.
rescuePrompt: Expand only Show next check. Read its time and stop without submitting the form.
try:
1. In desktop Chrome, follow the practice desk link in this chapter. If it downloads the page, open that file in Chrome. Start with Show next check folded.
2. Choose Ask Gemini and submit the practice request. Review the proposed action, permit only the requested expansion and read the time.
3. Fold the panel again. Ask for the visible waiting count without expanding it or submitting the form.

caption: Practice request
before: Every Friday at noon UTC remind me to count returned kits. Report the next scheduled weekday, the time with its zone and the exact reminder topic.
after: First run: Friday at 12:00 UTC is attached to counting returned kits. Second run: Friday at 13:00 UTC is attached to the same topic. The weekday stays Friday.
why: A time-zone label lets you compare the intended reminder with a device showing local time.
rescue: If noon comes back without a zone, ask for a check against UTC.
rescuePrompt: Read the saved task time, its displayed zone and the equivalent UTC time for the next run.
try:
1. Open Gemini and choose Task if the option is available to your account.
2. Enter the reminder once. Open the corresponding saved entry and inspect its weekday and time zone.
3. UTC is one shared clock. It lets you compare times from different places. Edit the saved time to 13:00 UTC. Check the schedule before removing the practice task.

caption: Practice request
before: Look at the two labeled buttons in the drawing. Which color goes with Review? Name the label and color you can actually see. Say unclear if the image is hard to read.
after: First run: Review is yellow. Second run: The Save button is blue. The hidden Review label cannot be read in the new view.
why: Covering a button tests the current camera view instead of memory of the first drawing.
rescue: If both labels are reported as visible, ask for a fresh look.
rescuePrompt: Describe only the uncovered label in the current camera view and give its color.
try:
1. Draw a yellow Review button and a blue Save button. In the Gemini mobile app open Live and point its camera at the drawing.
2. While sharing the camera view, speak the practice request. Compare its answer with your drawing.
3. Cover the Review button, leave Save visible and ask what label and color remain. Stop the camera after the reply.

caption: Practice request
before: Read the attached Count column. Give the sum, the number of known entries and the number of missing entries. How do you treat zero compared with a blank?
after: First run: 2 + 0 + 3 = 5, with three known and one missing. Second run: 2 + 0 + 4 + 3 = 9, with four known and none missing. The row containing zero still counts as filled.
why: Tracking known rows alongside the sum exposes a model that quietly discards zero.
rescue: If the first run has only two known rows, ask it to name the zero row.
rescuePrompt: List the four row labels with a number or the word missing. Count zero as known before adding.
try:
1. Create a sheet with Count values 2, 0, a blank and 3. Keep a row label next to each so the blank row survives. Attach it in a new Gemini chat.
2. Give Gemini the attachment question. Check each row used in its sum, including the recorded zero.
3. Replace the blank with 4 in a second file. Attach it in a new chat and repeat the count.

caption: Practice request
before: I must edit the formulas in an approved shared Excel workbook and verify the changed cells there. Compare a workbook-native helper with a detached chat using an exported copy. Which is the better starting point here?
after: First run: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Excel, when available to the account. Second run: A repository tool such as Codex, with a runnable importer test. The test runs against a saved sample file.
why: The location where the change must be verified can matter more than a general model ranking.
rescue: If the same tool is prescribed for both tasks, ask where the finished work lives.
rescuePrompt: Name the required artifact and its verification location for each job.
try:
1. Open Which tool for which job and expand the Spreadsheets decision table. Keep the result beside the actual job description.
2. Read the workbook job in the practice request. Use the spreadsheet table to choose the tool and verify why it fits.
3. A repository keeps project files and their saved history. A CSV is a plain-text table with a row on each line. Change the job to maintaining a tested CSV importer in a repository. Consult the Code table and name a repository tool instead.

caption: Practice request
before: My update log says the source guide renamed old.csv to new.csv on May 6. The saved book still says old.csv. Give a short dated note that names the changed file and where the old name still appears.
after: First run: The note says the source page changed its file name. The saved book still names old.csv. Second run: Both the source and the new book entry say new.csv. The history points to the affected page.
why: The two file names show exactly which instruction needs an edit. The date helps the next reader find that change again.
rescue: If the log says both files changed already, ask for the two names separately.
rescuePrompt: Which file name appears in the source guide and which file name is still in the book?
try:
1. Open What changed and look at the date and the linked page on one entry.
2. Give a new chat the update log. Look for both file names and the May 6 date.
3. Add a second note for May 7: the book now says new.csv. Ask for the updated history entry.

caption: Practice request
before: {{chapter.sections.2.prompts.0.text}}
after: First run: 0 + 2 + 3 = 5, three filled, one missing. Second run: 0 + 2 + 4 + 3 = 9, four filled, none missing. Row one holds zero in both runs.
why: An empty cell leaves the count unknown. A zero means someone recorded a count of none.
rescue: If the zero disappears from the filled count, ask to see each row.
rescuePrompt: Label all four cells filled or missing. Include a numeric zero among the filled cells.
try:
1. Find Count blanks in the Prompt library and start a new practice chat.
2. Send its request once. Record the total and filled and blank cell counts.
3. Replace blank with 4 in the four inputs and repeat the request.

caption: Practice request
before: I need two different reference lookups: reading a note through an approved connection, and repeating a job at a saved time. Which tag or chapter should I look for in each case?
after: First run: The connector tag leads to the Claude page for reading one item. Second run: The scheduled tag leads to the Gemini task page. That page shows where to check the next run.
why: A tag gathers related topics, while the page title identifies which product's controls you will use.
rescue: If the index leads only to general chat, ask for the feature name.
rescuePrompt: Identify the lookup term for a connected source and the term for a job with a repeat time.
try:
1. Open the book’s Tag index and expand connectors. Read the lookup request as your task.
2. A connector links two systems and controls what can pass between them. Follow the Claude connector entry and record the title it opens.
3. Return to Tag index. Find the Gemini scheduled task reference and record that page title.

caption: Practice request
before: Draft a handoff for a closed ticket and an open ticket. What format did I ask you to remember for practice handoffs? Say if you have no saved preference.
after: First run: The two ticket facts appear in bullets if the preference was retained. Second run: The new handoff also uses bullets if the saved preference is available. An unavailable preference is reported as unknown.
why: A second chat separates a saved preference from wording still visible in the first conversation.
rescue: If a new chat invents a preference, ask how it knows.
rescuePrompt: Identify the saved formatting preference if you can access it. Otherwise say unknown and leave the note unformatted.
try:
1. In Claude settings find Memory, if available. In a practice chat ask it to remember that practice handoffs should use bullets.
2. Ask for the ticket handoff in Claude. Check the reply against the formatting preference you entered.
3. Start another chat with memory available. Ask for a handoff about a delayed delivery. Inspect the memory setting afterward and remove the test preference.

caption: Practice request
before: Apply Ready list to these repair rows: bell ready, lens waiting, hinge ready. Which repair names pass the saved skill rule?
after: First run: Bell and hinge appear. Lens stays out. Second run: Bell and lens appear. Hinge now stays out.
why: Reversing two labels tests the saved rule more sharply than adding another ready item.
rescue: If the result is the original list twice, ask for a new sort.
rescuePrompt: Read the current status beside each repair name and apply the enabled Ready list rule again.
